lemma: Rank-r state DP. Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B, rank_Q(W) = r, t in Q^m, v in Z^m, T in Z, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Then #SAT(f) and every sign-atom count N(A) = #{x : ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j = A} are computable in time poly(m, n, r, log B) * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r).
gap: Open: (i) rank Theta(n) (G0002 regime, full-rank W with m = n^1.5): the state count (2Bn+1)^n is not sub-exponential, so no saving; (ii) the bit-size claim D a_j = O(r log(Bn)) needs an explicit Cramer bound stated in the review; (iii) this is probably the same object as S0017 (bounded-form pseudo-polynomial DP), so it is not a new method. Not a P vs NP step; no closure claimed. Review needed by a different session; confirms_closure not applicable (no open obligation recorded).
evidence: Exact check cm-3b1da622857b4a72 (physalis_code_run, 80 random instances, n in {6,8,10,12}, r <= 4): DP output equals brute force on all instances (0 mismatches); state count within (2Bn+1)^r on all instances (0 violations, max ratio 0.4). Exploratory computation only; it checks correctness of the DP, not the running time.
proved_step: PROOF. (1) Pick r linearly independent rows, M in Z^{r x n}. Each row satisfies W_j = a_j M with a_j in Q^r; let D be a common denominator so that D a_j is integral. For s(x) = Mx, W_j.x = a_j.s(x). (2) Hence [W_j.x >= t_j] = [(D a_j).s >= D t_j], so every gate, f and the atom sigma(x) depend on x only through s(x). (3) DP: N_0(s) = [s = 0]; N_{i+1}(s) = N_i(s) + N_i(s - M_{.,i+1}), exact integer arithmetic, N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : sum_k M_{.,k} x_k = s}. (4) After i steps every coordinate of s lies in [-Bi, Bi], so at most (2Bi+1)^r states, and at most 2^i states are reachable; total cost poly(m,n,r) times bit cost, which is O(r log(Bn)) bits for D a_j and D t_j (Cramer bound), giving poly * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r). (5) #SAT = sum_s N_n(s) [F(s) = 1]; N(A) = sum_{s: sigma(s)=A} N_n(s). Both read the same table. QED. CONSEQUENCE: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), time = poly * 2^{(1-delta)n} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. This subsumes the r-distinct-forms subclass S0027 (rank <= r there), with the new bound never worse.

statement: Coefficient bound for rank-r threshold evaluation. Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix of rank r>=1 with |W_ji|<=B, where B>=1. Choose r linearly independent rows M and r columns J such that M_J is nonsingular. For every row w_j of W, write w_j=a_j M over Q and put D=|det(M_J)|. Then D a_j is an integer vector and every coordinate has absolute value at most r r! B^r. Consequently, for any rational threshold t_j, the comparison w_j·x >= t_j for x in {0,1}^n is exactly equivalent to (D a_j)·(Mx) >= D t_j, and the latter can be evaluated with bit complexity polynomial in r, log(B+1), and the binary encoding length of t_j.
proof: Since the rows of M are independent and w_j is in their span, there is a unique a_j with w_j=a_jM. Restricting to columns J gives w_j[J]=a_j M_J, hence a_j=w_j[J]M_J^{-1}. Write q=det(M_J), so M_J^{-1}=adj(M_J)/q. Therefore D a_j=|q|w_j[J]adj(M_J)/q=sgn(q)w_j[J]adj(M_J), an integer vector. Each coordinate is a sum of r terms, each a product of one entry of w_j[J], bounded by B, and one (r-1)-by-(r-1) determinant of M_J, whose permutation expansion has at most (r-1)! terms each of magnitude at most B^(r-1). Thus each coordinate is at most r B (r-1)! B^(r-1)=r! B^r; the stated looser bound r r! B^r follows. Also D>0, so multiplying the inequality w_j·x>=t_j by D preserves its direction; w_j·x=a_j·(Mx), giving the claimed equivalence. Each coefficient D a_j has O(r log(r+1)+r log(B+1)) bits, each coordinate of Mx has O(log(nB+1)) bits, and exact rational comparison with Dt_j can be done using integers whose bit lengths are polynomial in these quantities and the input encoding length of t_j.
evidence: General determinant and adjugate argument above. Finite corroboration only: independent histogram-vs-brute-force verification cm-680af5c7f0c142f7 checked 22,506 generated cases; it does not prove the general lemma or an asymptotic speedup.
statement_start: Coefficient bound for rank-r threshold evaluation. Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix of rank r>=1 with |W_ji|<=B, where B>=1.

statement: Lattice-coordinate exact DP. Let M be an integer r-by-n matrix of rank r, and let H be an integer basis matrix for its column lattice L=M Z^n, so H is nonsingular and every column M_i equals H g_i for a unique g_i in Z^r. For each coordinate k set A_k=sum_{i=1}^n |(g_i)_k|. For any Boolean function F determined by threshold comparisons of rows W_j=a_j M with rational thresholds t_j, the number of x in {0,1}^n with F(x)=1 is computed exactly by a DP over z=sum_i g_i x_i, evaluating F from Mx=Hz. The DP visits at most product_{k=1}^r(2A_k+1) states and uses O(n times that bound) additions, plus polynomial bit complexity per operation.
proof: Initialize N_0(0)=1 and all other counts zero. For i=1,...,n update N_i(z)=N_{i-1}(z)+N_{i-1}(z-g_i), treating absent states as zero. Inductively, N_i(z) counts exactly the prefixes (x_1,...,x_i) with sum_{h<=i}g_h x_h=z: the two terms partition prefixes by x_i=0 or 1. Every coordinate z_k lies in [-A_k,A_k], so there are at most product_k(2A_k+1) possible states at each layer. At the final layer Mx=H sum_i g_i x_i=Hz; therefore every original threshold comparison, and hence F(x), is determined exactly by z. Summing N_n(z) over accepting z gives the desired count. Counts have at most n+1 bits; state coordinates and exact rational threshold comparisons have bit complexity polynomial in the input bit lengths and n.
evidence: Exact recurrence and state-range proof above. No finite computation is claimed.
statement_start: Lattice-coordinate exact DP. Let M be an integer r-by-n matrix of rank r, and let H be an integer basis matrix for its column lattice L=M Z^n

statement: Magnitude-independent DP for repeated scaled coordinate columns. Let r,t,q be positive integers and let M be the r-by-rt integer matrix whose columns consist of t copies of q e_k for each k in {1,...,r}, in any fixed order. For every function F:{0,...,qt}^r->{0,1}, the number of x in {0,1}^{rt} with F(Mx)=1 is computable exactly by a layered DP using at most (t+1)^r states per layer and O(rt(t+1)^r) integer additions. The state count is independent of q; arithmetic bit lengths are O(rt+log q). Here rank(M)=r and n=rt, so the result includes rank proportional to n when t is a fixed positive integer.
proof: Write column i as q g_i, where each g_i is some standard basis vector e_k and each e_k occurs exactly t times. Run the recurrence N_0(0)=1 and N_i(z)=N_{i-1}(z)+N_{i-1}(z-g_i), with absent states zero. Induction on i shows N_i(z) counts exactly the prefixes whose sum of g-columns equals z. At every layer, each coordinate z_k is an integer between 0 and the number of e_k columns processed, hence between 0 and t; therefore at most (t+1)^r states occur. At the final layer Mx=qz, so F(Mx)=F(qz) is determined by z and summing N_{rt}(z) over accepting z gives the exact count. Each count is at most 2^{rt}, requiring at most rt+1 bits; coordinates require O(log(t+1)) bits and computing qz requires O(log q+log(t+1)) bits per coordinate. Each transition uses a constant number of additions, proving the stated operation count and bit-size bound.
evidence: Exact recurrence, induction, and coordinate-range argument in the proof. No finite computation is claimed.
statement_start: Magnitude-independent DP for repeated scaled coordinate columns. Let r,t,q be positive integers and let M be the r-by-rt integer matrix

statement: Magnitude-independent DP with explicit evaluator cost. Let r,t,q be positive integers and M an r-by-rt integer matrix containing exactly t copies of each column q e_k (k=1,...,r). Let F:{0,q,...,qt}^r->{0,1} be supplied by an evaluator that, on any argument in this domain, uses at most T_F bit operations. Then # {x in {0,1}^{rt}: F(Mx)=1} can be computed exactly using at most O(rt(t+1)^r) integer additions and (t+1)^r evaluations of F, with all integers having O(rt+log(qt)) bits. Thus total bit time is O(rt(t+1)^r * (rt+log(qt)) + (t+1)^r T_F), up to polynomial indexing overhead. The rank is r and n=rt.
proof: For each column write M_i=q g_i, where g_i is a standard basis vector and each basis vector occurs t times. Define N_0(0)=1 and N_i(z)=N_{i-1}(z)+N_{i-1}(z-g_i), treating absent states as zero. Induction on i proves N_i(z) counts exactly the prefixes with sum of g-columns z. At every layer, coordinate z_k lies in [0,t], so at most (t+1)^r states occur. At the final layer Mx=qz, so evaluating F(qz) for each final state and summing N_{rt}(z) over states with F(qz)=1 gives exactly the desired count. Each transition performs a constant number of additions per state; each count is at most 2^{rt} and hence has at most rt+1 bits. State coordinates and qz have O(log(qt+1)) bits. The stated time follows by charging the declared T_F for each final state and standard polynomial bit cost for additions and indexing.
evidence: Exact recurrence, induction, coordinate range, and final aggregation prove correctness; the evaluator cost is charged explicitly. No finite computation is claimed.
